name: Treaty with the Kaskaskia, etc., 1832 (Treaty of Castor Hill with the Kaskaskia and Peoria)
nations: with the Michigamea, Cahokia and Tamaroa bands of the Illinois nation
promises: Article 4: 150 sections west of Missouri, including the Peoria village, ceded to the combined Kaskaskia and Peoria 'forever, or as long as they live upon it as a tribe'.
Article 5: an annuity of $3,000 for ten years, paid on their land in money, goods or stock at their choice, free of transport.
Article 6: cash payments to the Peoria and Kaskaskia to quiet the Peoria claim that they never understood the 1818 treaty of Edwardsville as ceding their Missouri lands.
Article 1 (the Kaskaskia side): the Kaskaskia ceded the lands secured to them by the 1803 treaty of Vincennes, except about 350 acres near Kaskaskia kept for Ellen Decoigne.
today: The Kansas land granted here, with the adjoining Piankeshaw and Wea grant of October 29, 1832, makes up Royce Areas 326 to 328. The four tribes united and ceded most of it by the treaty of May 30, 1854; the Indian Claims Commission's finding that the United States mishandled the sale of that land belongs to the 1854 treaty (kappler-644). No ruling, Act of Congress or government admission that this treaty's own terms were broken was found.

openQuestions: treaties.json error: both this entry and kappler-390 list all four tribes (Kaskaskia, Peoria, Piankeshaw, Wea) and the same Royce areas 326 to 328. This treaty was made with the Kaskaskia and Peoria only; the Piankeshaw and Wea signed the separate treaty of October 29, 1832. presentDayTribes also lists the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma, which was not a party; the successor is the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma.

Royce Areas 326 to 328 are the Kansas land the United States granted by these treaties, not land the tribes ceded. What the Kaskaskia and Peoria ceded here (their 1803 reserve in Illinois and claims in Illinois and Missouri) is not on the queue's areas for this entry.
Whether the ten-year annuity and the Article 6 payments were made was not researched.
No account by the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma about this treaty was found in this pass.
